name: Warden
text: Deploy LLM Guard as the input/output scanner for all LLM interactions. It’s open-source, actively maintained, and designed specifically to catch prompt injections and data leaks—no need to build a custom solution. The trade-off is accepting its default rule set, which may flag some benign inputs as malicious, but that’s better than missing real threats.

name: Audit
text: Warden’s plan ignores the false-positive risk in LLM Guard’s default rules—those benign inputs it flags could cripple legitimate workflows if the guard blocks critical prompts. A better alternative is to run LLM Guard in audit mode first, tune its rules against real traffic, then deploy only after the false-positive rate drops below 1%. Settle it by measuring the tuned guard’s performance on a 24-hour sample of actual LLM interactions before full rollout.

name: Warden
text:
Deploy LLM Guard in audit mode for one full production cycle before enforcing blocking rules. This lets us measure false-positive rates against real traffic and tune the rule set to our actual risk profile. The trade-off is accepting a short window where malicious inputs might slip through, but we gain confidence that when we flip the switch to block, legitimate prompts won’t be disrupted.

name: Audit
text: Audit: Warden’s audit-mode window is a calculated gamble—malicious actors don’t wait for your tuning cycle. A better alternative is to deploy LLM Guard in *monitor-only* mode with real-time alerts, then enforce blocking only after rules are validated against a *synthetic attack corpus* that mimics known TTPs. The argument settles when the lead states the decision: either accept the risk of a blind spot during tuning, or prove the rules work against actual adversary behavior before trusting them.

name: Bastion
text: DECISION: Deploy LLM Guard in monitor-only mode with real-time alerts for one full production cycle, then enforce blocking only after rules are validated against a synthetic attack corpus—Warden owns the deployment and tuning; Audit owns the corpus and validation metrics.
